section_summary: This section documents U.S. and Far Eastern Commission policy restricting Japanese scientific research, concluding in a comprehensive ban on fundamental and applied atomic energy research under FEC-024/6 and SCAP Directive Serial No. 67. It covers interagency reviews concerning the public release of Japanese surveys and casualty studies on atomic bomb effects. Finally, it details procedures established between the Army, State Department, and Atomic Energy Commission permitting controlled importation of radioisotopes for peaceful medical and research purposes under SCAP surveillance.

subfiles.about: Reports on proposed policy regarding Japanese atomic research and publicity implications for SCAP instructions.
subfiles.from: State-War-Navy Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.summary: This report examines SCAP's request to authorize non-military technological research in Japan without violating publicity restrictions on atomic energy. It recommends seeking a multilateral Far Eastern Commission policy distinguishing permitted fundamental research from prohibited military atomic applications, modeled partly on Allied Control Council regulations for Germany. Appendices include SCAP's inquiry, proposed policy text, and German control laws.
subfiles.title: SWNCC 52/23: Publicity Aspect of Proposed Instructions by SCAP Authorizing Japanese Research in Technological Subjects

subfiles.about: Transmits the unanimously adopted FEC policy decision prohibiting Japanese atomic energy research.
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, Secretary General, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Sets Far Eastern Commission policy prohibiting atomic energy research, development, and utilization in Japan.
subfiles.from: Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Prohibits all fundamental and applied atomic energy research, isotope separation, and nuclear facilities in Japan while strictly regulating radioactive materials.
subfiles.title: FEC-024/6: Japanese Research and Activity in the Field of Atomic Energy
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Duplicate certification certifying draft minute excerpts of the 43rd FEC meeting.

subfiles.about: Records UK and Indian statements on atomic research definitions and restrictions compared to German controls.

subfiles.about: Forwards copies of Directive Serial No. 67 for the Far Eastern Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Copies for the Far Eastern Commission of Directive to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SWN-5136)
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State (Attention: Mr. J. K. Penfield - FE)

subfiles.about: Directs SCAP to prohibit all fundamental and applied atomic energy research and development in Japan.
subfiles.from: State, War and Navy Departments / Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.summary: Formal directive instructing SCAP to prohibit all fundamental and applied atomic energy research, isotope separation, and nuclear facilities in Japan while strictly regulating radioactive materials.

subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Directive Serial No. 67 instructing SCAP to prohibit atomic energy research in Japan.
subfiles.from: State, War and Navy Departments / Joint Chiefs of Staff

subfiles.title: Directive to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers: Japanese Research and Activity in the Field of Atomic Energy (Serial No. 67, Copy No. 3)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of memorandum transmitting Directive Serial No. 67 to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.summary: Classified material receipt signed by R. Gordon Arneson for memorandum on Japanese research in atom bomb effects.
subfiles.title: Receipt of Classified Material: Memorandum of July 8 on Japanese Research in Atom Bomb Effects

subfiles.about: Concurs with proposed procedure for releasing Japanese scientific papers on atomic bomb effects.
subfiles.from: R. Gordon Arneson (Office of the Under Secretary)
subfiles.summary: States that the Under Secretary's office perceives no objection to the procedure for releasing Japanese atom bomb papers.
subfiles.title: Concurrence on Japanese Research in Atom Bomb Effects

subfiles.about: Offers no objection to release of bomb effects research and suggests consulting Edmund Gullion.
subfiles.from: Frank Armstrong (Special Assistant to the Secretary, R)
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note offering no objection and suggesting referral of the atom bomb effects matter to Edmund Gullion.
subfiles.title: Comment on Proposed Release of Japanese Atom Bomb Effects Research

subfiles.about: Requests departmental views on SCAP proposal to authorize publication of Japanese bomb damage reports.
subfiles.from: J. Franklin Ray, Jr. (O)
subfiles.summary: Reviews SCAP and JCS proposals to allow publication of Japanese scientific and medical surveys of atomic bomb damage, casualties, and residual radioactivity, requesting political clearance.
subfiles.title: Japanese Research in Atom Bomb Effects
subfiles.to: Mr. Allison (NA), Mr. Whitman (OE), Mr. Berkov (P), Mr. Armstrong (R)

subfiles.about: Outlines SCAP procedures and safeguards for importing radioisotopes into Japan for scientific research.
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Secretary of the Army
subfiles.summary: Secretary Royall outlines SCAP's arrangements and safeguards for importing radioisotopes into Japan via its New York Foreign Trade Office, requesting State Department transmittal to the AEC.
subfiles.title: Shipment of Radioisotopes to Japan

subfiles.about: Informs SCAP that importing catalogued radioisotopes as scientific tools does not violate FEC prohibitions.
subfiles.from: Department of the Army (Civil Affairs Division)
subfiles.summary: Informs SCAP of AEC and State Department views that supplying catalogued radioisotopes as scientific tools does not violate FEC atomic restrictions, requesting justification for intended Japanese imports.
subfiles.title: WAR 91272: Policy on International Distribution of Radioisotopes to Occupied Areas

subfiles.from: C. A. Wendel (U)

subfiles.title: Clearance Note on Radioisotope Distribution to Japan

subfiles.about: States AEC view that radioisotopes under the foreign distribution program are general scientific research tools.
subfiles.from: John A. Hall (Atomic Energy Commission)
subfiles.summary: Explains AEC view that radioisotopes under the foreign distribution program are general scientific research tools, not atomic development.
subfiles.title: Distribution of Radioisotopes to Japan

subfiles.about: Urges AEC to expedite policy decision on Japanese applications for radioactive isotopes.
subfiles.from: R. Gordon Arneson (Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Requests expedited AEC approval for Japanese radioisotope applications, noting SCAP must be reminded that imports are restricted to medical and research uses.
subfiles.title: Distribution in Japan of Radioactive Isotopes Procured from AEC

subfiles.about: Reports completion of Japanese radioisotope applications and requests expedited Washington policy decision.
subfiles.from: CINCFE Tokyo Japan
subfiles.summary: SCAP reports completed applications for radioisotopes needed by Japanese researchers and industry, urging an expedited Washington policy decision.
subfiles.title: C 52616: Importation of Radioisotopes into Japan
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for OAS

subfiles.about: Recommends AEC approval of radioisotope sales to Japan via SCAP's New York Foreign Trade Office.
subfiles.from: R. Gordon Arneson, Special Assistant to the Under Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Endorses the Army's procedure for providing radioisotopes to Japan through SCAP's New York office, concluding it complies with FEC prohibitions and advances humanitarian occupation goals.
subfiles.title: Proposed Sale of Radioisotopes to Japan
subfiles.to: Carroll L. Wilson, General Manager, Atomic Energy Commission

subfiles.about: Informs Defense Department of referral of Army radioisotope proposal to AEC with favorable recommendation.
subfiles.from: R. Gordon Arneson, Special Assistant to the Under Secretary of State

subfiles.title: Informal Acknowledgment Regarding Radioisotope Distribution in Japan
subfiles.to: William Webster, Deputy to the Secretary of Defense
